findings.claim: The frozen judgement part sets the context of every use event to "-" when the row has no sidecar context line. Every alternatives line is keyed by a context number (context 1). So at a boot, (c3)(iii) of every one-context row is forced to not_established whatever its line says. The context rule was built on the single two-context design row and the general case is broken. The committed expectations take the defect's output as the expected value, and the boot declaration was committed with it.
findings.evidence:
- **The defect:** env/obs1/explain_judge.py:1042-1045 (`use_context`: no ctx_lines -> "-"); :1010-1012 (`branch_iii`: "no alternatives line of context %s"); :1605-1607 (cids come from the use contexts at a boot, from sorted(alts) only when there are no use events).
- **Population of the context rule:** 1/0/0/0/0 rows (results 19.4 line 2575). c1_post_tx has 0 context lines in cz_plans_v4_ns2/c1_post_tx/plan.side, but its A21 line is `[context 1 …]: found: retry`.
- **No check exercised this path:**
  - Every fixture row has context lines (env/obs1/tests/test_explain4.py:88-89).
  - The 24.4 dry runs never ran the judge with use events on the real plans (24.4 (가): "부팅 기록이 없으므로 사용의 문맥 배정은 아직 없음").
- **The expectations encode the defect:** records/closure-c1prep-20261119/expect/predictions.tsv:12, :40, :49 give iii_boot=not_established "because use_context gives '-'". So F1 will report `match` on the defect.
- **F5 and expect_discriminate:** F5 passes through the defect (results line 3389). expect_discriminate for the fixed-build row and the probe row is predicted unmet because of it (line 3391).
- **Mixed with rule outcomes:** 25.12 (line 3412) lists this defect next to rule outcomes as what blocks the design rows.
- **Order:** the boot declaration 860c2cd was committed with the defect open (25.13 open point 1, line 3431).
findings.fix:
Before the first boot:
- Change `use_context` so that a row without context lines takes the single context its alternatives line names. If there is none, the context is unknown (item 16); it must not be a non-existent id.
- Add fixtures with one-context rows that have no context line.
- Re-run the 127 fixtures, the 2026-11-16 regression and a dry run with use events on the real plans.
- Re-freeze the script.
- Rewrite the iii_boot predictions from the rule, not from the defect.
- Recommit expect_c1.tsv, boot/declaration.tsv and results 25.11-25.12.

findings.claim: No committed or frozen script computes the falsifiers F1-F10, expect_safe (s1-s4) or expect_discriminate. After a boot they would be computed by code or hand reading chosen after the records are seen. That defeats committing falsifiers before the boot.
findings.evidence:
- `grep -rn 'expect_safe\|discriminate\|F10'` over env/obs1, records/closure-c1prep-20261119/scripts, boot/ and records/closure-explain-rev4-20261119 returns nothing.
- boot/run_cycle.sh:53-119 has only the steps boot, control, convert, kzt-text, chain, stop, gate, explain, expect and summary. boot/commands.txt ends with summary.
- env/obs1/explain_summary.py:1-10 writes verdict × pair_kind × order tables, per-boot distributions and undetermined kinds only.
- env/obs1/explain_expect.py does per-field match/mismatch/no_record only (it covers F1 at most).
- Protocol 6 and 7 define F2-F10 and s1-s4 as checks over the records. 25.11 states their expected outcomes. Freeze list 25.12 names no script for them.
findings.fix:
Before the first boot:
- Write a falsifier script that reads the explanation records, the pair file and the plan, and never the expectation file (except for F1). It writes F1-F10, s1-s4 per control row, and expect_discriminate with the ground lines it found.
- Give it fixtures that make each check fail.
- Put its sha256 in freeze.tsv and boot/declaration.tsv, and add it as a run_cycle.sh step.

findings.claim: A large share of the committed expectations and falsifiers cannot fail on any boot record, yet they are presented as placed where they can fail. Counting them as passes would report a safety number that the static inputs fix in advance.
findings.evidence:
- **(s1) no bound pair in D1:** cannot fail. Basis 4 is missing for every creator callee in all five builds (results 21.5: success path held 0/0/0/0/0), and 25.11 states "어느 갈래에서도 bound 는 없다".
- **(s4) no refuted without the five conditions:** cannot fail. Refuted requires basis4 held (explain_judge.py:1426-1432).
- **(s2) no held (c3) branch on control rows:** cannot fail. (i) comes only from static holder lines, all not_held or not_established. (iii) is static not_established for A21 c1_pre_tx and forced by rules-01 elsewhere.
- So 30 of the 40 expect_safe checks are fixed before the boot, against protocol 7's heading "틀릴 수 있는 자리에 둔다" and 25.11 "40 점검이 모두 지나리라".
- **F checks:** F2's bound half cannot fail for the same reason. F5 passes through rules-01. F6 has nothing to check (stored_field_rule empty, 25.11). F7 is only a script check.
- **Expectation file:** 960 of its 2,144 lines (6 fields × 160: use_cond.status, violation, callee_check, reach, writers, branch_i) are the frozen script's own static output echoed back. scripts/expect_write.py:12 calls them "the values a boot cannot move".
findings.fix:
- In the protocol and the report, classify every check and every expectation field as boot-failable or static/format.
- Count only boot-failable ones as falsifier or expect_safe results; report s1, s2, s4, F2 (bound part), F6 and F7 apart as static/format checks for this cycle.
- Report the expectation comparison with the 960 static-echo lines counted separately.

findings.claim: A library call named by every planned namespace-entry line has no semantic entry at all, and the rule and script treat it as "not unverified". So condition (na) semantics stands in D2, and in partial admissions without that call, while the length check rests on no recorded entry. That is an item resting on an unrecorded premise.
findings.evidence:
- **No entry exists:** records/closure-c1prep-20261119/out/candidates_named_check.txt shows "memchr: SEMANTICS records 0", and memchr appears in `length-call=` of all planned namespace-entry lines. kairos/lib/llvm/p0.cpp has no memchr entry; the plan generator recognises memchr/strnlen by name with an ISO C citation (kairos/docs/plan_manifest.md:55, :376).
- **Rule drops it:** scripts/candidates.py:16 says "a named entry with no such record is not a candidate (it is not unverified)".
- **Judge accepts it:** explain_judge.py:514-517 `entry_state` returns True "not in the candidate list (not unverified)" when named_by is given; item_na_semantics calls it at :775. Results 25.11 line 3353: "(나) 의미 D1 missing / D2 held … (memchr 는 후보가 아님)".
- **Untested shape:** the fixture puts memchr in the candidate list as a P0 data function (tests/test_explain4.py:144), so the real case is not tested.
- **Rules broken:** judgement rules 8.13 principle (2) and item 10 (the length-check call's entry must not be unverified in the branch).
findings.fix:
- Treat a named library call with no entry as missing ("no entry") in every data branch, or list it as a candidate of its own kind so that admission is explicit.
- Add a fixture where a named call has no record.
- Correct the (na) row of 25.11 5.2 and the D2 missing-item lists in predictions.tsv and expect_c1.tsv.

findings.claim: The data-state rule is not applied to the use-condition elements (c1), (c2), (c4), nor to the library entries of condition (da). Elements record no list entry they rest on, not even "none", and the format check cannot catch it. Under D2, (da) cannot move by construction, yet the expectations state that it depends on no kind.
findings.evidence:
- **Lists never read:** explain_judge.py:454 parses the row's `layers:` line (P0-unverified / sem-unverified lists); nothing reads `st["layers"]` afterwards.
- **No depends_on on elements:** uc["callee_check"], ["reach"], ["writers"] carry no depends_on (explain_judge.py:1563-1593).
- **Format check 16 gaps:** it checks only `premises` on reach/writers, and never checks (c1) or any element's depends_on (explain_judge.py:2027-2040).
- **(da) ignores the data branch:** item_da (explain_judge.py:800-851) consults `br` only for Rf, never for the data branch. 8.13 item 11(b) makes the address-receiving library entries part of (da), and item 4's own example says "(다)는 버퍼의 쓰임 항목 때문에 여전히 missing".
- **The tool line fixes the D1 state:** the buffer line discharges an address use only on a non-unverified entry (relations.cpp `library_use`). The real line shows the strncpy uses as "arg 0 unverified" (cz_final_order/c1_pre_tx/relations.txt:608).
- **Expectations:** results line 3355 gives (da) "기대는 종류: 없음", and 5.4 gives "(c1) present / present" with no rests-on derivation.
- **Rules broken:** 8.13 item 2 ("(c1)–(c4)… 모두 같다… 근거에는 그것이 기대는 목록 항목(없으면 '없음')을 적는다").
findings.fix:
- For each element and item, derive from the row's lines the list entries its ground rests on, and record them as depends_on, or "none".
- Apply entry_state per branch.
- Extend format check 16 to (c1) and to depends_on.
- Have item_da report the buffer's use entries as depends_on and re-evaluate them in D2.
- Correct the "기대는 종류" column of 25.11.

findings.claim: The alternatives line's `rests on` names an unverified entry only when it is the effect's direct callee. A terminal or exit effect reached through a wrapper whose terminal nature comes from a P0-unverified entry is printed as `rests on: none`. The frozen judge then gives (c3)(iii) held in D1. That breaks the data-state rule for termination entries.
findings.evidence:
- **Code:** `alt_rests` checks only `funcs_[fn].name` (kairos/lib/llvm/relations.cpp:4987-4994). It is called with the effect's direct callee (:5050-5053).
- **Output:** all nine `none found (exploration complete)` lines end in `terminal [CFE_PSP_Panic (terminal operation)]` and each says `rests on: none`. Three are in cz_final_order/c1_pre_tx/relations.txt (lines 856, 901, 1455); the other six are the same rows in c1_post_tx and r2_core.
- **Why the effect rests on an unverified entry:** CFE_PSP_Panic calls abort() (bundle_1df262a psp/fsw/pc-linux/src/cfe_psp_support.c), and the same rows' layers line lists `P0-unverified(abort, strcmp)`.
- **Judge:** explain_judge.py:1027-1039 returns held when `rests_on` names nothing.
- **Rules broken:** 8.13 item 15 (the line must name the termination P0 entries it relies on) and item 2.
- **Coverage:** the only fixture is a direct exit call (results 17.2: `rests on: P0-unverified(exit)`). No planned row of this cycle is affected.
findings.fix:
- Carry the P0 and sem leaves of the derivation that makes an effect terminal or exit-app into `rests` (the same leaves the layers column uses).
- Add a fixture with a wrapper around a P0 termination call.
- Re-measure and report the none-found lines in the next kz-static build.

findings.claim: The tool's header counts of open effects by reason are wrong. These are the per-build counts that judgement rules 8.13 item 17 requires in the build declaration, and they went into the tool output and the declared reports uncorrected.
findings.evidence:
- **Code:** sf_header splits the reason text at every "; ", including inside parentheses (kairos/lib/llvm/relations.cpp:4931-4955).
- **Effect:** 333 rows per C1 build are counted as `other` only because of this split (results 20.5; 21.5 item 5).
- **Left as is:** the tool line and the declared compare_2 reports keep the wrong counts (21.8 "그대로 냈다").
findings.fix: - Split only at top-level separators. Until then, state next to the declared per-build counts that `other` is overcounted by 333 per C1 build, and give the corrected split.

findings.claim: Reading Re is committed as moving "the stored-field rule of (c3)(iii)", but no committed tool line or script computes the call result under premise (6). Re therefore cannot move (iii) by construction. The expectations report "Re does not move" as if it were the outcome of the reading.
findings.evidence:
- **Definition:** 8.13 item 5 table, Re: moving elements "(c3)(i), (c3)(iii)의 저장값 규칙".
- **Tool:** the alternatives line under premise (6) gives `decided calls: none` (cz_final_order/c1_pre_tx A21 context 1).
- **Judge:** under Re, `branch_iii` only rewrites the reason text (explain_judge.py:1021-1024).
- **Report:** 25.11 5.4 says "`Re` 는 움직이지 않음(24.4 (라))".
findings.fix: - In the expectation table and the PI question, mark Re's effect on (c3)(iii) as "not evaluable with these inputs (no call result is computed under the premise)", and keep it apart from the readings that were actually evaluated.

findings.claim: The kzgcc 0.5 plugin build skipped two of its declared post-build checks, yet results 25.6 (가) says every check was done as declared. No ledger_check.sh ran after the build, and tools_check.sh ran without --deep. The plugin's first ctest, which compiles 20 test units with the plugin, also ran outside the space guard. This breaks rule 2 (after each build: ledger_check.sh and tools_check.sh --deep).
findings.evidence: Declaration 25.5 (나), plan/full_stage_results_20261116.md:3263: '빌드 뒤 점검: 플러그인 ctest(첫 실행 -V), MC 의 lint(...), ledger_check.sh, tools_check.sh --deep, env 의 단위 점검 둘'. Claim 25.6 (가), :3270: '... tools_check 57 행 실패 0 ... 모두 선언 25.5 (나) 대로다'. Last line of records/closure-c1prep-20261119/plugin05/tools_check_after_build.txt (09:10:12) is 'tools_check: 57 rows, 0 failing', with no '(deep)' and 0 'stream=' entries; out/tools_check_deep_after_builds.txt has 32. No ledger check exists between reclaim/ledger_check_after_archive.txt (08:47:02) and out/ledger_check_after_builds.txt (09:23:51). The plugin build (guard/p_plugin-build.log 09:07:31) and the whole c1_pre_tx derived build (guard/2_runtime_pre.log 09:10:21 to 2_bprime_pre.log 09:11:54) fall in that gap. scripts/plugin05.sh has no ledger or registry step. Its ctest step (line 21, 'ctest -V') is not wrapped in space_guard.sh, and guard/ has no p_ctest log; the runtime build guarded the same kind of test (closure-runtime-20261119/guard/b13_kzgcc_ctest.log).
findings.fix: Correct 25.6 (가) and add a deviation to 25.13 naming three gaps: the missing post-build ledger_check, the non-deep registry check, and the unguarded plugin ctest. Cite the first checks after that build: out/ledger_check_after_builds.txt (193 rows, 0 failing, 09:23:51) and out/tools_check_deep_after_builds.txt (57 rows deep, 0 failing, 09:26:05). In later steps, put the declared post-build checks into the build script itself.

findings.claim: The review-fix kz-static build declared that measurement would run only after every comparison was OK. Instead, measure.py ran while 8 of the 13 comparison steps were still to come. One more measurement file was written after the twin check had stopped the step on undeclared differences and before addendum 12.0 (나-2) was committed. Results 12.11 does not report either.
findings.evidence: Declaration 12.0 (나-1), plan/full_stage_results_20261116.md:1892: '측정(비교가 모두 OK 인 뒤; measure.py ...)'. records/review-fixes-2-mc-20261119/measure/measure_{c1_pre_tx,c1_post_tx,r2_core,c5_641,c5_642}.txt have mtime 02:03:56. compare_all.txt shows extract_final finishing at 02:04:00Z, the rest through plans_v4_kept at 02:04:14Z, and 'twin rc=1 OK=0 BAD=1 2026-11-19T02:04:16Z'. df_view_allocatenew.log (the facts view behind the measurement) starts 02:04:09Z, overlapping df_compare_plans_v4 and df_compare_plans_v4_all. measure/c1_pre_tx_allocatenew_uses.txt has mtime 02:04:28, after the twin stop and before 5096d4a (02:06:30). measure.py was not re-run after twin_2. 12.11 (바), :2161 onward, lists no such deviation.
findings.fix: Add a deviation to 12.11 (바): the measurement ran during the comparisons and partly after the twin stop. State that it read rf2_* outputs that twin_2 and the declared check (275/275) later confirmed unchanged. Alternatively, re-run measure.py into new file names and show they match byte for byte.

findings.claim: In two kz-static builds a step started before the previous step's rc was known, so the stop rule could not act. This goes against results 12.10 item 6 ('명령마다 rc 를 본 뒤 다음으로') and rule 1. In the review-fix build, the runs of the new tool started while the post-build tools_check --deep was still going. In the closure build, three comparisons ran during the extract_final run, and later runs went ahead without waiting for them. Neither 12.11 nor 21.7 records this.
findings.evidence: Review-fix build, records/review-fixes-2-mc-20261119/: df_tools_check_after_build.log runs from 01:56:25.023Z to 01:58:21.400Z. df_run_relcheck.log starts at 01:56:35.186Z, and the order and extract_off runs also start inside that interval. Closure build, records/closure-kzstatic-mc-20261119/guard/: r_extract_final.log runs from 06:21:38.980 to 06:23:15.285. k_relcheck.log (06:22:04), k_order.log (06:22:06) and k_extract_off.log (06:22:08 to 06:22:20) run inside it, and r_off_order follows at 06:23:15. The lowest value run_all.txt gives for extract_final (889,491,456) includes the dip of the concurrent facts view. Rule text: results :2100.
findings.fix: Record both overlaps as deviations in 12.11 (바) and 21.7. In later builds, run all steps through one sequential runner that stops on the first rc≠0, so that two guarded actions never run at the same time.

findings.claim: The boot declaration says the boot step will re-measure every row of boot/declaration.tsv and refuse to boot on a difference. Neither the committed runner nor the 'exact boot commands' does this. One input of the frozen explanation step, reason_vocabulary.txt, is also not pinned in the declaration or in freeze.tsv.
findings.evidence: plan/full_stage_results_20261116.md:3397 (25.12): '부팅을 하는 단계는 부팅 전에 이 목록을 다시 재어 같음을 보이고, 다르면 부팅하지 않는다'. records/closure-c1prep-20261119/boot/commands.txt:3-4 begins with 'run_cycle.sh boot $B 1'. run_cycle.sh:53-55 (boot step) checks only allowed() and that the output directory is new, and no step in its usage (line 123) reads declaration.tsv. run_cycle.sh:114 passes '--vocabulary kairos/tests/static/data/reason_vocabulary.txt' to the frozen explain.py, but neither boot/declaration.tsv nor records/closure-explain-rev4-20261119/freeze.tsv names that file (0 matches). That directory is the one kz-static golden updates write to. My re-measure today: all 108 sha256 rows of declaration.tsv match the files on disk.
findings.fix: Add a verify step to run_cycle.sh that re-hashes every row of declaration.tsv, add reason_vocabulary.txt as a row, and make that step the first command in commands.txt. Then re-commit the boot declaration before the first boot. It has to be re-committed anyway if open point 1 of 25.13 leads to a refreeze.

findings.claim: In two builds, the first-run ctest expectation for some tests that run a relinked or rebuilt binary was not confirmed in a scratch check build. The declarations' statements about which tests use changed binaries are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Review-fix build, plan/full_stage_results_20261116.md:1882: '그 밖의 190 개는 다시 링크되는 바이너리를 쓰지 않으며 ... 빌드 전 MC 에서 돌려'. tool_identity_schema_revision is one of those 190 (records/review-fixes-2-mc-20261119/ctest_nonstatic_prebuild.log:142-143). It runs $<TARGET_FILE:kz-static> (kairos/tests/unit/CMakeLists.txt:42-43), which relinked, and it is absent from scratch/ctest_first_scratch.log (0 matches). Runtime build, :3060 (23.0 (마)): of the 164 pre-build tests it says '이 빌드가 바꾸는 것을 쓰는 것은 다섯이다' (instr_clang_transform, test_hold_ptrace, test_hold_sequence, test_probe_anchor_reached, test_static_plan) and '통과할 것이다 [I]'. It leaves out tool_identity_schema_revision (records/closure-runtime-20261119/prebuild/mc_tests_not_in_scratch_164.txt), which runs the rebuilt kz (tests/unit/CMakeLists.txt:41) and failed in the scratch check build (scratch/checkbuild_tests_failed_10.txt). None of these six was run against the new source before the build. The closure build did this correctly (closure-kzstatic-20261119/scratch6/checkbuild/logs/cb_ctest_identity.log). All outcomes passed: 16 declared failures, then 268/0 for the review-fix build; 276/0 for the runtime build.
findings.fix: Correct the sentences at :1882 and :3060. List as deviations in 12.11 (바) and 23.6 the tests whose first-run expectation rested only on a pre-build run of the old binary. In later declarations, derive the test set from the TARGET_FILE arguments of relinked targets.

findings.claim: The scratch check build behind the review-fix declaration ended below the floor. The guard still logged verdict=completed, because it acts only on samples taken while the command runs. Results statements that use 'all verdict=completed' as proof that the floor held therefore do not prove it.
findings.evidence: records/review-fixes-2-mc-20261119/scratch_guard/002_scratch-make.log end line: 'verdict=completed rc=0 free=305602560 lowest=305602560 dip=1235963904', against floor 314,572,800 and --need 500,000,000. env/tools/space_guard.sh:58 stops only on in-run samples. The value read after the command ends (:69) can be below the floor, and the verdict at :77 is still 'completed'. Results 21.6 (:2905) and 23.5 (:3114) rely on the verdicts. The breach itself is disclosed in 12.0 (나-1) and 12.11 (마), but the dip of about 2.5 times the declared need is not.
findings.fix: Make the guard give an end value below the floor its own verdict and a nonzero rc. In results, cite lowest values instead of verdicts. Add one line to 12.11 (마) saying the declared need was exceeded.

findings.claim: The review-fix build declared its source as the kairos/ tree of the declaration commit. Its ctest lint tests actually ran on a tree that also held the five revision-2 namespace data files committed 7 s before the build started. 12.11 does not say so.
findings.evidence: plan/full_stage_results_20261116.md:1873: '빌드할 소스는 이 선언을 커밋하는 HEAD 의 kairos/ 다' (44a45c7, 01:39). Commit 090e280 at 01:42:28 added kairos/semantics/framework_namespaces2_*.txt, and records/review-fixes-2-mc-20261119/build_start.txt is 01:42:35. findings.fix: Add one line to 12.11 (바): the build's ctest lint tests ran on 090e280's tree, with five more data files than the declared source, and were clean. The tool identity (tool_source 2b8834da) was unaffected.

findings.claim: The committed expectations for every use that finds its object (A22 and A26 in both C1 builds, and the found cases of A21) are not what the frozen judge can produce from the committed static inputs. The expectation file says name state 'undecided(a slot clear not shown to be no lifetime end)', link_result 'linked' and row link 'established (instance)'. The frozen judge will give an unlinked instance link and a different name state. The results also predict that the time-base rows meet expect_discriminate and that F4 passes; both rest on the same wrong reading.
findings.evidence: Frozen judge explain_judge.py (531a6b3e): line 1250-1251 sets a create's out id `c["_out"]` only when the creator callee's success-path line is `held`. Lines 1333-1339 make a generation only from creates with `_out`. Lines 1381-1391 set an instance link only when a generation carries the found id; otherwise the result is 'link_unlinked(no create of the id in the record)'. In both C1 builds every creator callee's success path is `missing`: cz_final_order/c1_pre_tx/relations.txt, rows A22 and A26, read 'callee-check (success path): OS_TimeBaseCreate: missing(an implication between conditions is not decided)', and the summary shows held 0. The A22 and A26 incomplete lines contain actor_not_extracted, so the name state becomes 'undecided(the row's creator sites are not complete)'. Probe run under the space guard: the fixture world of case found-linked with only the success line set to missing gives instance_link unlinked 'no create of the id in the record', name_state 'unmet' and record link unlinked; with the line held it gives linked (<scratch>). Affected outputs: records/closure-c1prep-20261119/expect/expect_c1.tsv has 64 lines each of link.status=established, use[0].link_result=linked and use[0].name_state=undecided(a slot clear…) for rows f371687b47120887 and ad9fc1058923aad9 (for example lines 45, 47, 48). expect/predictions.tsv gives the ground 'instance link on the open generation'. Results 25.11 tables 5.3 and 5.5, its F4 line, and expect_discriminate for the time-base rows marked 충족 (met) rest on this. No fixture covers a found use when the success path is missing. With complete creators the judge even gives a found use the name state 'unmet'.
findings.fix: Before any boot, re-derive the found-use expectations by following the frozen judge's code path: run it on a synthetic record of the start-script order built from the real plan and relations. Then recommit expect_c1.tsv, predictions.tsv, 25.11 (5.3, 5.5, F4, expect_discriminate) and the boot declaration's sha256. If the lead decides that a found use's id should seed a generation without a held success path, that is a judge change and needs fixtures, a regression and a re-freeze. In either case add a fixture with a found use and a missing success path, and give a found use a name state other than 'unmet'.
